title: Florida AG announces investigation into OpenAI over shooting that allegedly involved ChatGPT
description: ChatGPT had reportedly been used to plan the attack that killed two and injured five at Florida State University last April. The family of one victim has said that they plan to sue OpenAI over the incident.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: After data breach, $10B valued startup Mercor is having a month
description: After falling victim to a hacker, Mercor is facing lawsuits and reportedly losing big-name customers.
author: Julie Bort

title: Meta AI app climbs to No. 5 on the App Store after Muse Spark launch
description: The app was ranking No. 57 on the App Store just before Meta AI's new model launched. Now it's No. 5 — and rising.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Is Anthropic limiting the release of Mythos to protect the internet — or Anthropic?
description: Anthropic said this week that it limited the release of its newest model, dubbed Mythos, because it is too capable of finding security exploits in software relied upon by users around the world. Are real cybersecurity concerns a cover for a bigger problem at the frontier lab?
author: Tim Fernholz

title: Google and Intel deepen AI infrastructure partnership
description: The two tech giants are looking to co-develop custom chips, at a time when demand for CPUs is high due to a growing global shortage.
author: Rebecca Szkutak

title: Sierra’s Bret Taylor says the era of clicking buttons is over
description: Last month, Sierra launched Ghostwriter, an agent designed to build other agents. With this “agent as a service” tool, the startup intends to replace traditional click-based web applications with natural language. Users simply describe what they need, prompting Ghostwriter to autonomously create and deploy a specialized agent to execute the task.
author: Marina Temkin

title: Amazon CEO takes aim at Nvidia, Intel, Starlink, more in annual shareholder letter
description: Andy Jassy's annual shareholder letter reads something like a diss track to a wide range of competitors as he defends spending $200 billion in capex.
author: Julie Bort

title: Final 2 days to save up to $500 on your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 ticket
description: Ticket discounts of up to $500 will end tomorrow, April 10, at 11:59 p.m. PT. After that, prices for TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 go up again. Miss this, and you’ll be paying more for the same access to one of the most anticipated tech epicenters of the year. Register now to lock in these savings.
author: TechCrunch Events

title: Poke makes using AI agents as easy as sending a text
description: Poke brings AI agents to everyday users via text message by handling tasks and automations without complex setup, apps, or technical know-how.
author: Sarah Perez

title: AWS boss explains why investing billions in both Anthropic and OpenAI is an OK conflict
description: AWS has an ingrained culture of handling coopetition, he explained, because the cloud giant also competes with its partners.
author: Julie Bort

title: Tubi is the first streamer to launch a native app within ChatGPT
description: Tubi becomes the first streaming service to offer an app integration within ChatGPT, the AI chatbot that millions of users turn to for answers.
author: Lauren Forristal

title: Astropad’s Workbench reimagines remote desktop for AI agents, not IT support
description: Astropad’s Workbench lets users remotely monitor and control AI agents on Mac Minis from iPhone or iPad, with low-latency streaming and mobile access.
author: Sarah Perez

title: OpenAI releases a new safety blueprint to address the rise in child sexual exploitation
description: OpenAI's new Child Safety Blueprint aims to tackle the alarming rise in child sexual exploitation linked to advancements in AI.
author: Lauren Forristal

title: Databricks co-founder wins prestigious ACM award, says ‘AGI is here already’
description: Matei Zaharia has won the top honor from the Association for Computing Machinery. Now he's working on AI for research and says AGI is simply misunderstood.
author: Julie Bort

title: Final 3 days to save up to $500 on your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 pass
description: Save up to $500 on your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 pass until April 10, 11:59 p.m. PT. Secure your spot at the center of the tech ecosystem. Register here.
author: TechCrunch Events

title: Atlassian launches visual AI tools and third-party agents in Confluence
description: Confluence users can now create visual assets within the software in addition to new third-party agents working with Lovable, Replit, and Gamma.
author: Rebecca Szkutak

title: Google quietly launched an AI dictation app that works offline
description: Google's new offline-first dictation app uses Gemma AI models to take on the apps like Wispr Flow.
author: Ivan Mehta

title: I can’t help rooting for tiny open source AI model maker Arcee
description: Arcee is a tiny 26-person U.S. startup that built a high-performing, massive, open source LLM. And it's gaining popularity with OpenClaw users.
author: Julie Bort

title: Firmus, the ‘Southgate’ AI data center builder backed by Nvidia, hits $5.5B valuation
description: Nvidia-backed Asia AI data center provider Firmus has now raised $1.35 billion in six months.
author: Julie Bort

title: Intel signs on to Elon Musk’s Terafab chips project
description: Intel will join SpaceX and Tesla in an effort to build a new U.S. semiconductor factory in Texas, although the scope of its contributions are unclear.
author: Tim Fernholz

title: Anthropic debuts preview of powerful new AI model Mythos in new cybersecurity initiative
description: The new model will be used by a small number of high-profile companies to engage in defensive cybersecurity work.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: Uber is the latest to be won over by Amazon’s AI chips
description: Uber is expanding its AWS contract to run more of its ride-sharing features on Amazon's chips. This is a thumb-of-the nose at Oracle and Google.
author: Julie Bort

title: Anthropic ups compute deal with Google and Broadcom amid skyrocketing demand
description: Anthropic bulked up its compute deal with Google and Broadcom as the company has seen its run-rate revenue surge to $30 billion.
author: Rebecca Szkutak

title: Google Maps can now write captions for your photos using AI
description: Google is rolling out new features to make it easier for users to contribute local knowledge to Maps. Most notably, Gemini can now create captions when users are looking to share a photo or video about a place.
author: Aisha Malik

title: 4 days left to save close to $500 on TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 passes
description: 4 days left to save up to $482 on your TechCrunch disrupt 2026 ticket. These low rates will disappear on April 10 at 11:59 p.m. PT. Register here.
author: TechCrunch Events

title: The AI gold rush is pulling private wealth into riskier, earlier bets
description: On a recent episode of Equity, we  talked to Arena Private Wealth to explore a growing trend: family offices bypassing VCs to gain direct exposure to AI startups, turning them from passive investors into active participants.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: AI startup Rocket offers vibe McKinsey-style reports at a fraction of the cost
description: Rocket's new AI platform combines strategy, product building, and competitive intelligence, aiming to move beyond code generation.
author: Jagmeet Singh

title: OpenAI alums have been quietly investing from a new, potentially $100M fund
description: Zero Shot, a new venture capital fund with deep ties to OpenAI, is aiming to raise $100 million for its first fund. It has already written some checks.
author: Julie Bort

description: Google's new offline-first dictation app uses Gemma AI models to take on the apps like Wispr Flow.
author: Ivan Mehta

title: Iran threatens ‘Stargate’ AI data centers
description: Iran said it will target U.S.-linked data centers with new missile strikes, as the war between the U.S. and Iran escalates.
author: Rebecca Szkutak
